convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I've been writing letters I'll never send. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
Aki shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
Another crack. The telling doesn't hold together anymore.
They talked. Everything changes now.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Please — I can't shake it. I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. I need help. Please."
"Rest won't touch this. The heat's climbing and my head's full of cotton. Someone who knows what they're doing — please."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
Another pass over the same ground. Somebody's being careful. Careful people leave cleaner trails — and cleaner trails are still trails.
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
Counted.
"Still on that favor."
"Let me sit with all that. We'll pick it up later."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"We never finished talking about their secret — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'They fill the quiet. Anyway — where was I?'"
Done — their story has a crack in it now.
They talked. Everything changes now.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
"Okay, that's my quota of socializing."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
If we don't write it down, it didn't happen. I'm writing it all down.
Another pass over the same ground. Somebody's being careful. Careful people leave cleaner trails — and cleaner trails are still trails.
Counted.
"I wrote down what happened today. All of it. The boring parts too — future scholars will thank me."
"A hundred years from now someone should know we were here and what it cost."
"Still on what they want."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about their secret — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Aki has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"We went over this," Aki says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
Aki looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"You know what, fair." Aki nods slowly. "I can see how that looked. But here's the thing..." And the thing is mundane, and verifiable, and fine.
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"I've got things to do. People to avoid. You know."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Can we talk?" Lidya sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
"I stay out of it. Mostly. It's getting harder."
"Still on what's been happening."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Can we talk?" Lidya glances around first. "People are saying things. About you. Is any of it true?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
A beat. Then, as if shaking something off:
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Everyone's choosing sides and pretending they aren't. I hate it."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"As I said — Still on what's been happening."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"The pantry's nearly bare. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. I know the creek bend, past the treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know what I did in the raid? I stood down Big-Eyes at the treeline — it ran. Don't call it brave. Call it awake."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

deathBeat: d16: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Hazel Cisse is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d16: 🕯️ Hazel Cisse is dead — starvation. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d16: The village's quarrel was with Hazel — and Hazel is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
recoverHome: d17: That night, they bring Hazel home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d16: At the grave, Aki speaks for Oliver — "Hazel trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d16: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d16: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."
d16: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "The audience wants an encore. A trial, then — smaller this time, but televised." Haul 1,000 kcal to the pantry within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.

d16: ◈ ARC III — ENGINES. SYSTEM: "VIEWERSHIP MILESTONE. Organic unit demonstrates compounding capability. Resonance protocols unlocked." — Your gifts deepen. Used in sequence, they resonate. The village is no longer just surviving. It is becoming something.
d16: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 51. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 4."
d16: SYSTEM: "Organic units require fuel. Noting. Noting loudly. The audience is very quiet, which for them is screaming."
d17: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.
d18: 📺 SYSTEM: "We have already cleared your morning. You are welcome. We require 300 kcal of tubers and your full attention. The fans love a cooking segment."
d18: SYSTEM: Codex and inventory overlay online.

d19: ◈ CRISIS — THE FIRST GRAVE. Aidan is dead. The village digs its first grave, and everyone understands at once: this place can kill you. It just did.
